entries.title: About jspassgen | Security Architecture and Principles
entries.content: Skip to main content jspassgen 0.0.19 Menu GitHub Change color theme System About jspassgen jspassgen was created to solve a persistent vulnerability in modern authentication workflows: the reliance on proprietary, cloud-hosted, and telemetry-heavy password generators. Design Principles Zero External Dependencies: The core generator library contains zero third-party packages, preventing software supply chain compromises. Local Trust Boundary: Passwords never touch a network socket. All entropy is derived from hardware noise via operating system CSPRNG interfaces. NIST SP 800-63B Compliance: Full adherence to modern digital identity guidelines, discouraging arbitrary composition rules in favour of length and entropy. Post-Quantum Preparedness: Hardened key derivation primitives designed to resist future quantum acceleration. Author & Maintainer Created and maintained by Sebastien Rousseau. Dual licensed under Apache-2.0 and MIT.

If an adversary attempts to authenticate with any canary decoy, an immediate intrusion alarm triggers before the genuine master key is exposed. THE PHILOSOPHY Legacy password generators measure length.We measure informational entropy. For three decades, software forced users into artificial composition rules: one uppercase letter, one digit, one symbol. Modern cryptanalysis and GPU clusters crack these predictable patterns in seconds. jspassgen eliminates superstitious rules in favour of Claude Shannon's information theory, post-quantum KDF primitives, and client-side memory safety. Every secret is mathematically verified before it touches your clipboard. ENGINEERING CAPABILITIESBuilt with cryptographic purity and zero assumptions. Hexagonal isolation, hardware-bound entropy, and verifiable mathematical models engineered for uncompromising long-term security. 01 / QUANTUM HARDENINGResilient against tomorrow's compute. Protects credentials against future quantum decryptors and massively parallel ASIC cracking arrays. Under Grover's algorithm, quantum search provides quadratic speedup (O(√N)), meaning 256 bits of symmetric entropy provides 128 bits of post-quantum security. Paired with memory-hard Argon2id and HKDF expansion, brute-force search remains computationally infeasible.
